JOHNNY ISAKSON.name: Johnny Isakson
JOHNNY ISAKSON.background: Born December 28, 1944, in Atlanta; University of Georgia graduate; Georgia Air National Guard 1966-1972 (staff sergeant). Real estate executive: opened Northside Realty's first Cobb County office and was president of his own real estate firm 1979-2001. chairman of the Georgia Board of Education 1990-1992; Georgia State Senate 1992-1996; U.S. House, Georgia's 6th District, 1999-2005 (first elected in a 1999 special election); U.S. Senate 2005-2019. Won a third Senate term in 2016: 447,661 votes (77.5%) in the May 24 Republican primary over Derrick Grayson and Mary Kay Bacallao, and 2,135,806 votes (54.8%) in the November 8 general over Democrat Jim Barksdale (41.0%) and Libertarian Allen Buckley (4.2%). Disclosed a Parkinson's diagnosis in 2015 and ran anyway; announced August 28, 2019 he would leave for health reasons and resigned effective December 31, 2019. Died December 19, 2021.
JOHNNY ISAKSON.ideology: AJC (May 2016) said he mixes conservative credentials with a willingness to reach out to the left; his 2016 primary opponents Grayson and Bacallao tried to outflank him on the right. Roll Call (2021) called him "among the most universally beloved senators on Capitol Hill" and host of "perhaps the best bipartisan event of the year." President Biden wrote that he "put country before party, and valued building consensus over political combat" (American Legion, 2021).
JOHNNY ISAKSON.record: also sat on Finance; Foreign Relations; and Health, Education, Labor and Pensions. As Veterans' Affairs chairman he sat on the conference committee for the 2014 VA wait-time law, shepherded the 2018 overhaul of veterans' community care (VA MISSION Act), and made the benefit-appeals backlog his top priority (Roll Call). His Veterans Appeals Improvement and Modernization Act was signed August 23, 2017; the Senate also passed the VA Accountability and Whistleblower Protection Act (signed June 23, 2017) and the Harry W. Colmery Veterans Educational Assistance Act ("Forever GI Bill," signed August 16, 2017). The 2020 veterans law H.R. 7105 was named the Johnny Isakson and David P. Roe, M.D. Veterans Health Care and Benefits Improvements Act (signed January 2021).
JOHNNY ISAKSON.notes: Deceased (Dec. 19, 2021); the page should present him historically. H.J.Res. 46 date not given on the page (Senate vote was in 2019). S. 2372's introduced text carries a different short title than the header; it was the Senate vehicle labeled VA MISSION Act. He's my friend. He's my partner.").
